transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-07
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Clarke (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jamal Rivera (Head of InfoSec, Solstice), Maria Alvarez (CTO), Heather Lin (DevOps)
---
Summary: discovery focused on security posture and deployment options for Redwood inference. Main topics: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, encryption and KMS integration, data retention and residency, hosted vs dedicated vs private network options, POC next steps.
Topics: security attestation, key management, network isolation, retention policy, demo/POC requirements
Action items (recorded in metadata)
---
[00:00] Ethan: Hi everyone thanks for joining, quick intros, Im Ethan from Redwood, and Priya is our systems engineering lead.
[00:15] Maria: Hi all Maria here, CTO, Jamal and Heather from our side. We're looking to understand security posture before we talk POC.
[00:23] Jamal: Yeah we have GDPR and PCI scoped products so encryption and retention are big for us. Also curious about audit logs and how much detail is captured per token request.
[00:35] Priya: Great, we usually start with our compliance artifacts. Redwood's hosted stack is backed by SOC2 Type II and we also maintain ISO 27001 controls, we can share the attestation summaries. For customers with stricter needs we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the network plane.
[00:55] Jamal: When you say Private, do you mean full on-prem or VPC peering? Clarify please.
[01:02] Priya: Sorry, yeah, private means a customer-managed control plane option — VPC connected private deployment or an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. With VPC we do a private control plane so the model serving runs in your subnet and traffic never crosses public internet except for control plane ops if you choose to.
[01:20] Heather: Do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning? We use Okta.
[01:26] Ethan: Yes SSO via SAML is supported, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and RBAC with role tiers. For Dedicated/Private you can integrate your IdP and we honor SAML assertions, map groups to roles.
[01:40] Jamal: How granular is RBAC? Can we separate token creation from model admin and billing?
[01:46] Priya: You can create custom roles, yes. We typically provide roles like admin, billing, model-deployer, app-service. Customers often create a restricted token role that can only call inference endpoints and nothing else.
[02:00] Maria: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs for access and request metadata retained for at least 12 months and exportable to our SIEM.
[02:09] Priya: Our platform emits audit trails for control plane actions and per-request metadata for inference calls. For hosted plans logs are streamed to secure storage, we provide a logs export API and can push to your cloud logging (e.g., CloudWatch, GCP Logging). For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and long-term export to your S3/GCS buckets.
[02:30] Jamal: Are logs tamper-evident? Hashing / WORM options?
[02:35] Ethan: We can enable append-only export to your bucket and recommend lifecycle and object lock policies in the customer's storage for WORM. We also provide signed delivery manifests.
[02:48] Heather: Encryption at rest and in transit, what KMS integrations do you support? We use AWS KMS and a customer HSM for some keys.
[02:56] Priya: We integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS natively, and for Private deployments we have a path to integrate with customer-managed HSMs via standard PKCS#11 or KMS proxy. For hosted, keys at rest are encrypted with provider-managed keys by default, but you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) on Dedicated with an envelope encryption pattern.
[03:20] Jamal: Does tokenization or redaction happen on any logs? We need PII removed from logs by default.
[03:27] Priya: We support redaction rules and can disable storage of full request bodies in logs; rather we store request metadata and hashes. For sensitive PII we recommend running through our prefix caching and client-side masking in the application layer, and in Private deployments you can pre-process before sending.
[03:45] Maria: What about data residency — can we guarantee that data for EU customers stays in EU?
[03:51] Ethan: Yes, we have region routing policies. For hosted we can pin workloads to a region and for Dedicated/Private you can keep everything in your region or on-prem. Note that some model variants may not be available in all regions; we'll surface compatible variants.
[04:10] Jamal: Observability and tracing — can we correlate inference requests back to internal request IDs? We need structured tracing.
[04:17] Priya: Absolutely, you can send an internal trace-id in the request header, and our tracing hooks include that id in logs and traces. We have OpenTelemetry integrations for export to your tracing backend.
[04:30] Heather: For the POC we want to run a small baseline showing latency and e2e encryption — any recommended config?
[04:36] Priya: Start with a small model variant on Dedicated with KV cache off then on, measure p95 latency. We'll share a sample benchmarking script. For e2e encryption prove the TLS handshake and KMS envelope flow in a short test.
[04:52] Maria: Are there common gotchas you see customers miss?
[04:56] Priya: A few — not accounting for warm-up costs on larger models, forgetting to bind trace ids so logs are less useful, and not scoping which tokens have deploy rights vs inference rights. Also SSO group mappings sometimes need iterative tweaks.
[05:15] Jamal: About SOC2 reports, can we get the full bridge letter or only summary artefacts for security review?
[05:22] Ethan: We usually share redacted SOC2 Type II report and a bridge letter where applicable. For enterprise we can sign an NDA and provide more detailed artifacts.
[05:34] Jamal: Can you describe your key rotation cadence and options?
[05:40] Priya: Key rotation is handled by the KMS provider for managed keys; for BYOK we recommend a rotation cadence per your policy — we support key rollover with minimal service disruption using double-encrypt key envelopes.
[05:54] Heather: On network egress controls, we need to restrict outbound to only certain CIDR ranges. Is that supported in Dedicated?
[06:01] Priya: Yes Dedicated and Private allow egress controls and we can configure outbound firewall/NAT rules in the customer subnet. For hosted we provide IP allowlists and private endpoints where possible.
[06:17] Maria: If we want to run an air-gapped on-prem deployment, what parts remain Redwood-managed, if any?
[06:25] Ethan: The on-prem package aims to be self-hosted; the control plane can be customer-managed. We do an initial deployment assist and handover to your Ops. Optionally we can run a support channel but no external control plane traffic if you choose full air-gap.
[06:40] Jamal: Licensing and support SLAs — do you have SOC2-backed SLAs or enterprise support add-ons?
[06:46] Ethan: We have enterprise support tiers with SLAs and an optional compliance add-on that includes extended artifact retention and priority response.
[06:55] Heather: One specific ask: we need per-token provenance to satisfy audits. Can you attach key ids and model version to each request log line?
[07:03] Priya: Yes we include model version, model hash, key id reference, and token counts in the request metadata we log. We can make the fields configurable in Dedicated/Private.
[07:20] Maria: Is there any chance of generating PII in model outputs that would leak through logs?
[07:26] Priya: Model output capture is optional; by default we store only truncated outputs for quality monitoring. For PII-sensitive workloads we recommend disabling output capture and running local post-processing or filtering.
[07:42] Jamal: Ok, timeline — assuming we like the artifacts, we aim to run a 4 week POC. What does Redwood need from us to start?
[07:50] Ethan: Typical POC ask — list of sample prompts, a representative data subset, expected success criteria (latency threshold, quality metrics), and a contact for infra to do network prep. We will supply a perf test harness and onboarding checklist.
[08:05] Maria: On retention, we have legal requiring a max of 30 days for raw request traces but 7 years for audit confirmations. How do you accommodate dual retention windows?
[08:15] Priya: We support tiered retention. For hosted we can configure short-term request body TTL and separate long-term audit exports. For Dedicated/Private you can set lifecycle rules: keep raw request bodies short-lived, persist audit summaries long-term in your storage.
[08:35] Jamal: What about data deletion requests — e.g., right to be forgotten. Do you support deletion of specific records?
[08:41] Ethan: For Hosted we can facilitate deletion requests and mark data as deleted in logs and storage. For Dedicated/Private it's under customer control and we provide tooling and APIs to find and delete request artifacts.
[08:55] Heather: Any pen test or third-party attestation reports we can review?
[09:00] Ethan: We can share pen test summaries and risk remediation notes under NDA.
[09:07] Maria: Ok let's talk tradeoffs briefly — hosted easiest but less control, dedicated predictable and regionally isolated, private gives full control but more ops. Any nuance for performance vs cost?
[09:18] Priya: Exactly. Hosted is quickest and good for low-friction start but may have multi-tenant characteristics. Dedicated gives you reserved pools and lower variable cost at scale, better latency SLOs. Private puts you in the driver's seat but increases ops. Also quantization/throughput choices can change unit costs.
[09:42] Jamal: For our security review, we'll want a network diagram and data flow map.
[09:47] Ethan: We'll provide a standard architecture diagram and tailor it for your VPC layout.
[09:54] Priya: Also pro tip: for tests, include a real JWT or trace id in a header so the logs we generate look identical to your prod traffic.
[10:05] Maria: Any known limitations around KV cache and sensitive data being resident in GPU memory? We need guarantees that cached prefixes are not persisted beyond TTL.
[10:16] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral in memory on the serving nodes and not written to disk by design. For extra assurance on Dedicated/Private we can disable cross-request caching or set aggressive TTLs and evictions.
[10:30] Jamal: How do you handle model rollouts and potential regressions?
[10:35] Priya: We support canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. Redwood Optimize can run quality monitors against prompt sets and send regression alerts tied to those prompts.
[10:50] Heather: Ok can you summarize what artifacts you'll send?
[10:54] Ethan: SOC2 Type II redacted report, ISO summary, network architecture template, onboarding checklist, sample perf script, and the security deck. Priya will attach the benchmark script.
[11:05] Maria: Great. Anything we missed?
[11:09] Jamal: One more: do you have a data processing addendum and standard DPA?
[11:14] Ethan: Yes we have a DPA and standard data processing terms; legal can sign or negotiate as needed.
[11:21] Priya: Quick note on implementation: for BYOK we ask for key rotation windows early so we can coordinate.
[11:28] Heather: Thanks everyone. Well review and come back with the dataset and compliance checklist.
[11:35] Ethan: Thanks all, we'll turn around the artifacts by Thursday and propose a follow-up deep dive with networking and SRE.
[11:42] Maria: Bye
[11:43] Jamal: Thanks
[11:44] End of recording.
